Topic T1 · First Impression

What You'd Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item A1 is a small stainless hex washer head screw with two features you can spot before you ever read the print: the orange coating on the threads and the wide washer formed under the head. Take a few moments to review and examine the part.

As received: stainless hex washer head, a coarse thread, and the orange coating on the threads.
The sample on a grid, with its SBS label. Each grid square is 5 mm — handy for judging size.

Hex Washer Head — an unslotted hex head with an integral flange (washer) formed under it. The “UHW” in the part number. Stainless steel throughout.

Epoxy-Lock Patch — the orange thread-locker coating. It starts at the tip and covers the thread, leaving 2–3 bare threads under the head. The “EPOX” in the part number.

Plastite Thread — a trilobular, double-helix thread that forms its own thread in plastic — not the common machine screw thread.

18 mm Washer O.D. — the integral washer under the head measures 18 mm across. The “18” in the part number.

What Is a Plastite Thread?

Trilobular Double Helix

Plastite threads are a special trilobular (three-lobed), double-helix thread used in plastic applications.

How It Forms the Thread

Three lead edges form or flow a thread through the plastic base material rather than cutting it. Friction points sit at the three lobes; the relief areas between them leave room for displaced plastic.

Reading “48-2”

The 48 is the thread angle (48°). The 2 says the thread is a double helix.

Topic T4 · Material & Passivation

18-8 Stainless Steel, Passivated

The “S” in .68N25UHWS/PR18EPOX calls out the base material. Here is what it means — and why this stainless part needs no plating.

Requirement

Material: stainless steel · Grade: 18-8 (A2) · Finish: Passivated

Reading the “S”

When a part number or description does not state a material, a reasonable assumption is plain steel — about 90% of global fasteners. If it does say stainless, 18-8 is the reasonable default unless specified otherwise.

What “18-8” Means

18-8 is the American term for a common stainless grade containing about 18% chromium and 8% nickel, equivalent to type 304 (A2).

Cost vs. Plated Steel

Stainless steel screws typically cost two to four times more than an electro-coated carbon steel equivalent.

Why Stainless Here

This part is used on a watercraft, where the environment would be too corrosive for a plated steel part.

Passivation: The Finish on Stainless

What It Is

A cleaning of the stainless steel that removes contaminants and free iron which may have been deposited during cold heading or roll threading.

What It Does

The cleaning enhances the passive (chromium oxide) layer — the layer that makes stainless steel stainless. It is a barrier between the metal and its environment, improving corrosion resistance.

No Plating Needed

Stainless steel screws do not require a plating or finish for most corrosive environments — so passivation is the finish listed in the item attributes.

Proof on Paper: The Wire Certificate
The wire maker’s EN 10204 3.1 inspection certificate — Kuang Tai Metal Industrial, stainless steel wire, 5.63 mm. Part of the PPAP package (T8).
Chemistry for heat 5H272: Cr 17.15% against a 17.00–19.00% spec, Ni 8.05% against 8.00–10.50% — the 18-8 make-up. Tensile strength 508 N/mm².

Topic T5 · Epoxy-Lock Thread Locker

The Orange Epoxy-Lock Patch

The “EPOX” at the very end of the part number calls out a thread locker applied to the threads — in this case an epoxy lock, supplied in orange.

Requirement

W/EPOXY-LOCK (ORANGE) — START AT TIP AND COVER WITHIN 2–3 THREADS UNDER THE HEAD, TO PRINT # 203000485 REV AA.From the extended description. “Within 2–3 threads under the head” means the coating stops short, leaving a few bare threads next to the head.

Where It Goes

Applied over the entire length of the thread, starting at the tip, except 2 to 3 threads under the head.

How You Spot It

A hard orange coating on the threads — clearly visible in the sample photo on the first slide.

Where It Is Called Out

Controlled by a note on the customer print (note 9 for this part), and repeated in the extended description.

What the Print Says
The notes block of the BRP print (click to enlarge): “ND Industries Epoxy-Lock coating, applied over the entire length of the thread except 2 to 3 threads under the head.”
Thread Locker Certification
ND Industries — Certification of Conformance for this part.

What the Certification Proves

Process: ND Epoxy-Lock (R) Orange on part 68N25UHWS/PR18-EPOXY, quantity 20,000, specification per customer. The certificate states that the parts conform to the blueprint or specification for the locking element only.

A certificate on the thread locker is a standard piece of a PPAP package — see .

Topic T6 · Per Print Parts

Defined by a Drawing, Not a Catalog

The “/PR” in the part number means per print. That one tag changes how the part is made, documented and controlled.

What “Per Print” Means

The part is defined by either a customer or supplier drawing. It is not a standard or catalog part.

Not Off the Shelf

Per-print parts need to be manufactured with custom tooling and are not available off the shelf.

Words Are Not Enough

A per-print part cannot be defined with a description alone — unlike a part made to a consensus standard or catalog design, which can be ordered by description or catalog number.

Document Controlled

All per-print parts are document controlled in P21, with the print linked to the item.

Revisions & Deviations

Revision AA

The print is linked at revision AA. It has been updated about 27 times since it was first released in 2009. The last revision, in 2018, added our part to the print.

Major or Minor

A revision can be major (a dimension or feature changes) or minor (a note is added or clarified).

When a New Revision Arrives

Find out whether SBS has inventory worldwide or parts on order with a supplier. A print change may make that material non-conforming to the update.

Deviation

In that case we negotiate with the customer to use the parts made to the old revision under a deviation.

Topic T8 · PPAP Documentation

The Approval Package Behind This Part

Class 5 told us this is a PPAP Level 3 part. Here is what that means, where to find the documents, and what is inside.

What PPAP Is

PPAP — Production Part Approval Process — is widely used in the automotive industry. The supplier provides samples and technical documents to the customer for approval.PPAP: the standard proof package a supplier submits before shipping full production.

The Handshake

If the customer is happy, they sign the PSW (Part Submission Warrant) and return it to SBS. The signed PSW acknowledges the parts were made to specification and may go to mass production, as long as everything in the PPAP is followed.

Customer PrintInspection ReportsMaterial CertsThread-Locker CertificateProcess Flow ChartFMEAControl PlanGauge R&RPart Submission Warrant
Finding the PPAP File

Search SharePoint

PPAP documents are on SharePoint. Search the SBS part number or, more likely, the customer part number — 250001070 for this item.

Can't Open It?

If you cannot access the folder, submit an IT ticket or talk to Quality.

The file: 250001070-5-29-18_BRPQUE_LVL3.pdf — the PPAP submitted to the customer in 2018.
What a PPAP Contains
The PPAP Submission Requirement Checklist.

Typical Contents

  • A customer print
  • Inspection reports from both SBS and the manufacturer
  • Chemical composition and mechanical properties of the raw material
  • A certificate on the thread locker
  • A process flow chart of the manufacturer’s steps
  • An FMEA, a control plan and a Gauge R&R report
Inspection Evidence
SBS dimensional results — PPAP Level 3, every feature measured against the print: PASS.
The manufacturer’s own inspection report — Shin Mone Screw Co., Ltd., measured against the print limits.
Process Documents
Process flow chart — the steps the manufacturer will follow, from receiving wire to finished screw.
FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) — all the things that could go wrong in manufacturing, and how each failure is prevented or detected.
Control Plan & Measurement System
Control plan — how the parts will be inspected and deemed conforming.
Gauge R&R — a statistical report showing the manufacturer can measure the parts effectively and consistently.
The Part Submission Warrant
The PSW — customer BRP Queretaro S.A. de C.V., supplier Specialty Bolt & Screw Inc., tier 2 manufacturer Shin Mone.
The signature block — the signed PSW is effectively a handshake between SBS and the customer.

Reference

Glossary

Every code and term used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's "jump" button to see it in context.

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

A common stainless grade, roughly equivalent to type 304, with about 18% chromium and 8% nickel. When a part number says stainless and nothing more, 18-8 is the reasonable assumption.

BRP

Bombardier Recreational Products — the customer whose print controls this part. Only users logged in with SBS or BRP credentials can see the part on the E-Catalog.

Deviation

A customer-approved agreement to use parts made to an older print revision after the print has changed.

Epoxy-Lock

The ND Industries thread-locking coating applied to this part’s threads, supplied in orange. The “EPOX” at the end of the part number.

Family Print

A customer print or drawing that controls more than one part — typically similar parts, listed in a table.

FMEA

Failure Mode and Effects Analysis — a report of everything that could go wrong in the manufacturing process and how each failure is prevented or detected.

Gauge R&R

Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility — a statistical report showing that the manufacturer can measure parts effectively and consistently.

Passivation

A cleaning of stainless steel that removes contaminants and free iron left by cold heading or roll threading, strengthening the protective chromium oxide layer.

Per Print (/PR)

A part defined by a customer or supplier drawing rather than a standard or catalog design. It needs custom tooling and cannot be defined by words alone.

Plastite 48-2

A trilobular, double-helix thread-forming thread for plastic. The 48 is the thread angle; the 2 means a double helix.

PPAP

Production Part Approval Process — the documentation package a supplier submits to prove its process can reliably make a part to print before full production begins.

PSW (Part Submission Warrant)

The signed cover document of a PPAP package — the formal sign-off that the part is approved for production.

Thread Forming

A screw that forms (flows) its own thread in the mating material instead of cutting it. The “N” in the part number marks a thread cutting or thread forming screw.

Trilobular

A three-lobed cross-section. The three lead edges form the thread through the plastic, while relief areas between them leave room for displaced material.
